correctness.rationale: The 72-facet complex is reconstructed exactly. Four-vertex support minimality follows from the unique integral \(2\)-cycle relation on the boundary of a tetrahedron. Exhaustion gives exactly \(60\) missing tetrahedra. Two explicit integer cocycles evaluate every such boundary as \(\pm e_1\) or \(\pm e_2\), and both coordinate directions occur. Since the published topology gives \(H_2(K;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^2\), the evaluation map is a surjective homomorphism \(\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb Z^2\) and hence an isomorphism, proving every shortest boundary nonzero and primitive and proving the exact two-class \(30/30\) distribution. Two explicit simplicial generators close to a \(240\)-element facet-preserving group whose orbit is all \(60\) supports.

value.rationale: Minimum vertex support of a nonzero integral middle-homology class is a natural combinatorial systolic invariant. Here the full minimum layer is classified, every carrier is primitive, only two rank-two homology rays occur with equal multiplicity, and the \(240\)-element symmetry is transitive on all carriers, forcing the two rays into one symmetry orbit. This connects local four-vertex geometry with the product manifold’s middle homology and symmetry rather than reporting an arbitrary finite count.
